schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The post-build gate: python FILTERS that judge orient's measurements and red a build whose component fails one. Founding filters (cairn/build_inspector/inspector.py): `charter_on_disk` — code with no intention+why.json; `proofs_exist` — code with zero proofs (Law 8); `silent_device` — a BaseDevice subclass that never calls emit() outside proofs (the MAP.md:434 claim, enforced); `state_is_projection` — state.json must equal project(history.json), the drift check half of the compiled-view IOU. `inspect(component=...)` gates one build; `inspect()` is the whole-repo sweep. CLI exits 0 clean / 1 findings — gate-able by anything that reads an exit code. Inference-free by construction: no deepen seam exists here; a gate that consults an oracle is not a gate.
why: Akien, 2026-07-27, verbatim: 'the next thing is a post build inspector (also in python with FILTERS) that can catch these kinds of things. we find a new thing, we add a new filter. can also be a seperate, command line only inference free operation to run it on the whole repo once built. we should only ever have to do that once.' The deeper why is his older observation that CC does not add logging (and its kin) until told — 'i have been resigned to the fact that we wouldn't have such logging until some lever presented itself... and a post build inspector is just the thing.' The lever is Law 4: a discipline in CC's habit is policy; a filter at the build gate is physics. 'Only once' holds by construction — the sweep brings the existing tree to the gate one time, then every build passes through the inspector, so wanting a second sweep is itself a finding (a build bypassed the gate).
invoke: import: `from cairn.build_inspector import inspector`. Prove: `python3 cairn/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py`. Gate one component: `python3 -m cairn.build_inspector.inspector <component>`. The sweep: no argument.
node_class: device (gate) — class-space tooling; no runtime state, no daemon; fires at the build event, never on a clock.
entry: FRESH build, orient's first child. Deliberate reuse on the record: orient's device_census is the measuring layer under every row-judging filter — the first evidence on orient's edge (e) (scans-vs-filters as a shared library), earned by use. The registries stay separate: a scan MEASURES, a filter JUDGES.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter.
how_it_learns: THE POINT — 'we find a new thing, we add a new filter.' Every filter carries the failure that seeded it as Provenance in its docstring (tooth 10 refuses a filter nobody was taught by). Founding set: charter_on_disk ← orient's census flagging its own missing charter (2026-07-27); proofs_exist ← the true-but-silently-partial bus record (2026-07-25); silent_device ← zero emit() sites in bus against MAP.md:434's 'no device can opt out' (2026-07-27); state_is_projection ← CLAUDE.md's compiled-view IOU, the drift-check half. Growth rule: a failure Akien catches that a filter could have caught becomes a filter, and the class stops recurring (Law 1).
filed_edges: (a) THE GATE IS NOT YET WIRED TO THE BUILD EVENT — today CC runs it; the lever lands when the tester (or a hook) refuses a PROVEME crossing whose component reds the inspector. That wiring retires the 'CC runs it by discipline' gap, which is the same gap the inspector exists to close — tracked, not resting.

(b) the sweep's findings are WORK ITEMS, not the gate's business: five silent devices filed at CairnCommons/troubles/silent-devices-2026-07-27.json; the inspector reds, the owner disposes (no-enforcer — gated ownership).

(c) candidate filters seeded but unbuilt: stale-'on purpose' comments (device.py:36's transient-absence-written-as-intent — needs a checkable shape first); host-seam seal expiry; charter answers how-does-it-learn (the learning-as-a-pattern IOU).
(d) CLAUDE.md's awaiting-physics entry for the compiled-view rule can name this filter as its drift check once (a) lands — the entry retires only when the gate fires without CC choosing to run it.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_inspector.py (12 teeth) under the tester. Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a healthy component draws a finding (a gate that always fires gets unwired — tooth 1); (2) a seeded failure fails to fire exactly its filter (tooth 2); (3) a hand-edited state.json passes (tooth 4 — the drift check's whole claim); (4) inspecting a nonexistent component returns clean instead of refusing (tooth 7 — a gate that inspects nothing passes everything); (5) a filter enters FILTERS without provenance (tooth 10); (6) an oracle or outbound import appears in inspector.py (tooth 12). WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: if a second whole-repo sweep is ever genuinely needed, the gate is not gating — that need is itself the loudest finding.
proof: proofs/test_inspector.py — each founding filter pinned fire-and-stay-quiet on a synthetic tree; door-written voyages clean, hand-edits caught with diverging keys named; repairs go through the door; refusals loud; findings complete on first pass; real tree by invariant. Green: `python3 cairn/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py`.
owner: CC owns the code + proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the design (filters, only-once sweep, inference-free — his ruling 2026-07-27) and the disposition of findings on components he owns.
provenance: Born 2026-07-27, minutes after orient PROVED, as orient's first child — Akien: 'go go go!'. Its first sweep (16 components) found 6: its own missing charter (this file is the fix — the second instrument in one day whose first act was to catch its own builder) and five silent devices, filed as the trouble above.
